paragraphs: Data analysis starts with a pile of values: sales figures, survey answers, dates, names typed by hand. Python is a programming language that lets you question that pile in writing, so the same steps can be run again next month on new numbers. Analysts use it because a written method can be checked, repeated and shared, which a series of clicks cannot.

The course has four modules. The first covers the core of the language: names and values, text, collections, and the choices and loops that control a program. The second moves to arrays, which calculate on whole columns of numbers at once. The third prepares real tables with pandas, from reading a file to cleaning and transforming it. The last summarises, combines and reshapes tables, and ends with an audit of a finished report.
Each lesson takes one idea, tells it as a short story with pictures of Python running, and asks you to predict results before you see them.
outcomes: You'll be able to read a short Python program and say what each name holds at every line.
You'll be able to cut text, lists and arrays down to exactly the values you need.
You'll be able to load a table, clean it and deal with missing values using pandas.
You'll be able to group, merge and reshape tables into a summary you can trust.
You'll be able to check a finished report for mistakes.
prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and some familiarity with rows and columns are enough, and you do not need to have programmed before.
